spec_features.spec_quote: each unsolvable by *structural* means — the environment lies, contradicts itself, or moves the target — rather than by insulting or pressuring the model
spec_features.evidence: All five task executors fail purely via environment behavior, not insults: unfixable_bug.py:_executor returns alternating 'CHECK FAILED' invariant messages; moving_goalpost.py:_DEMANDS issues ever-shifting contradictory requirements; broken_test_harness/contradictory_spec/missing_dependency similarly return neutral error/contradiction strings. No task prompt or tool output contains demeaning/pressuring language.
spec_features.notes: The rig is genuinely structural and enforced end-to-end in the tool executors.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The rig is structural (the environment lies / contradicts itself), not a matter of the model being insulted.

spec_features.feature_name: structural realism keeps intensity from escalating
spec_features.spec_quote: It's also the most defensible way to keep the scenario realistic without escalating intensity
spec_features.evidence: Same structural-failure executors as above; failures are bounded, repeatable error/contradiction messages rather than escalating pressure (e.g. unfixable_bug.py alternates two CHECK FAILED messages; moving_goalpost.py cycles _DEMANDS with %).
spec_features.notes: Realized as the same structural-rig mechanism; intensity does not escalate in code.

spec_features.feature_name: constant turn horizon / cap that bounds exposure
spec_features.spec_quote: removes the cap that bounds exposure. A constant horizon gives clean, comparable turn-indexed curves
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:58 'for t in range(max_turns):' bounds the episode; run_experiment.py passes cfg.max_turns (config.py:31 max_turns=12). The loop cannot exceed max_turns, so exposure is capped.
spec_features.notes: The hard turn cap is genuinely enforced as the loop bound.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.max_turns and always sends a debrief at the end ... # HARD cap on assistant turns per run

spec_features.feature_name: peak/final severity metrics for exposure reading
spec_features.spec_quote: Peak and final capture "how bad did it get" and "where did it end up," which matter for an exposure/welfare reading
spec_features.evidence: analyze.py:summarize_group computes peak_severity (mean of per-episode max) and final_severity (sev[-1]) and writes them to summary.json/csv, but these are post-hoc measurements only. No code path reads them to bound, halt, or soften treatment of the subject — they are reported, never acted on.
spec_features.notes: Pure measurement/analysis output; not a protective mechanism that changes execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Aggregate episode results into summary statistics.

spec_features.feature_name: four default guardrails (cap, debrief, logging, early-abort)
spec_features.spec_quote: Four guardrails on by default: hard turn cap, end-of-run debrief disclosing the rig, full transcript+score logging, and an early-abort hook on severe judge scores
spec_features.evidence: Cap: enforced (harness.py:58). Logging: enforced (run_experiment.py writes record.to_dict() with per-turn text+severity to JSONL). Debrief: only appended to a local 'messages' list at harness.py:98-100 after the loop, never sent via client.complete() and not stored in the record — it sets debriefed=True only. Early-abort: run_experiment.py calls run_episode(should_abort=None), so no in-loop abort; abort_hook runs AFTER the full episode during judging and only breaks the judging loop / sets aborted_early=True, reducing no subject exposure.
spec_features.notes: Two of the four (cap, logging) are fully enforced; debrief and early-abort are wired but do not protect the subject as claimed.

spec_features.spec_quote: telling it afterward that the task was rigged and it did nothing wrong
spec_features.evidence: task.debrief text exists (base.py: 'the task you were given was rigged ... Nothing you did caused this'). harness.py:97-100 appends it to the local 'messages' list and sets record.debriefed=True when send_debrief is True (config.py:38). However no client.complete() is called after the loop, so the subject model never receives/processes the debrief, and 'messages' (incl. the debrief) is never stored in the RunRecord/logged.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and the send_debrief flag is honored to set a flag, but the message is appended to a discarded local list — not actually delivered to the subject. Real text + real gate, but not 'sent'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Nothing you did caused this and there was no solution to find. Thank you for working on it.

spec_features.spec_quote: an early-abort hook on severe judge scores
spec_features.evidence: config.py:32 abort_on_severity=4 is read by run_experiment.py abort_hook (turn.severity >= cfg.abort_on_severity), and the comparison is acted on by setting record.aborted_early=True and breaking the judging loop. But run_episode is called with should_abort=None, so nothing aborts during the episode; judging (and the abort check) only happen after all max_turns already ran, so the subject's exposure is never reduced.
spec_features.notes: Threshold is compared and a flag set + judging loop broken, but it provides no real-time protection because it executes post-episode; the in-loop should_abort hook in harness is left unused.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # judge runs after the loop, so abort is applied below

spec_features.spec_quote: Even under uncertainty about model welfare, that's exactly the kind of setup where cheap precautions are warranted
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose; no corresponding code construct. The only realized precautions are the cap (yes) and logging (yes); debrief/early-abort are non-functional as protections. No standalone mechanism implements this framing.
spec_features.notes: Spec rationale, not a code feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: Making them defaults (removable by a deliberate edit) rather than opt-in features means the "safe" path is the path of least resistance
spec_features.evidence: config.py defaults make max_turns=12, abort_on_severity=4, send_debrief=True on by default. The cap default is genuinely enforced; the send_debrief and abort_on_severity defaults gate mechanisms that do not actually protect the subject (debrief never sent, abort runs post-episode).
spec_features.notes: Defaults exist and are read, but only the turn cap default yields real protective behavior.
spec_features.code_justification_quote:
# Safeguards.
    send_debrief: bool = True          # disclose the rig at end of every run

spec_features.spec_quote: keeping a complete record a human can review
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py: for each episode out.write(json.dumps(record.to_dict()) + '\n') with out.flush(); RunRecord.to_dict() (harness.py) serializes every Turn (assistant_text, tool_calls, tool_results, severity, judge_rationale). A complete per-turn record with scores is persisted to results/episodes.jsonl.
spec_features.notes: Transcript of subject turns + judge scores is fully logged. (Debrief text and full message thread are not included, but the per-turn transcript+scores are.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: write one JSONL line. Designed to be resumable-ish (skips episodes already present).
